findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the front baffle of the ice machine to be soiled. Shown to the kitchen manager and she mentioned that the baffle will be cleaned. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation, as well as contamination of ice.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine’s sanitizing temperature was recorded between 151F - 154F. The PIC mentioned that the dish machine’s last service was about eight months prior to the inspection. Discussed with PIC that the minimum sanitizing temperature must be 160F to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces. Ensure that the dish machine is serviced to maintain a sanitizing surface temperature of at least 160F. Will follow-up on 9/17/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is an ice cream machine that is currently not in use in the kitchen area. The PIC mentioned that the facility does not plan to use the machine in the future. Remove any unused pieces of equipment if there is no plan for use in the future.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents could not be found during inspection. Copies of employee health documents were provided and discussed. Staff present at the time of inspection signed reporting agreements. One additional part time worker will sign a reporting agreement at their next shift. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Heat sanitizing dish machine final rinse surface temperature was observed below 160F. Final rinse temperature of water coming in at the manifold was at +190F according to digital readout of temperature gauge. Dish temp testers used by facility and inspector were placed through multiple ware washing cycles and were observed with a maximum temperature reading of 149.8F and 151.8F respectively. Inspector also used a thermolabel temperature test strip that did not change color after a full ware washing cycle. Test strip would turn black if surface temperature reached at least 160F. Call for service was made to maintenance during inspection. In the meantime, the dish machine may be used for the wash and rinse steps of ware washing with manual sanitization at the 3 part sink using quat solution (200-400ppm; contact time 30 seconds prior to air drying). Spot check will be conducted after dish machine is repaired to verify proper function. **See General Comments for additional information.**
After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through equipment that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a utensil surface temperature of 160F as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-bucket was observed at 100ppm. Solution was prepared earlier in the day and needed to be refreshed. A new solution was provided and again observed at 100ppm later during inspection. Another solution was prepared and observed at 200ppm immediately after dispensing once foam was allowed to settle out of solution. Ensure test strips are used to verify concentration of solutions prior to use. Consider also pre-wetting wiping cloths with sanitizer solution prior to storage in a fresh solution to help minimize absorption of chemical out of solution into wiping cloths.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine was observed with a food-contact surface temperature of 150F. The food contact temperature of items in the dish machine must measure 160F or higher when sanitized in the dish machine. The maintenance staff does not work on Fridays and the school is not open on Saturday and Sunday, so the follow-up will be conducted on 10/19/2022. 

4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71oC (160oF) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator; P (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans in walk in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
The two Continental walk through coolers in the kitchen are 50-54F. The one on the front service line has fruit that was just opened from a can at approximately 8:30-9AM and will be discarded by noon, is reading 54F on the outside thermometer and internal temp appears to be consistent. The cooler with two sides has an air temperature of 51F but has no potentially hazardous food held in it at this time, but it is reported that this cooler is often used. Service these coolers so that they are holding potentially hazardous foods at 41F or below at all times and do not use coolers until they are able to maintain at 41F or below. It was also discussed that the coolers should be added to temperature logs to make sure that they are being checked regularly. The walk in cooler will be used until these can be serviced. A spot check will be performed when school resumes in the Fall. 
750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed deli ham in the walk in cooler to be date marked 5/9. Ham had been used on deli sandwiches that were prepped for today's lunch as well.. Ham sandwiches and ham in the walk in were discarded during inspection to correct the violation. Make sure that potentially hazardous foods are not being used past the 7 days allowed.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
